result.title: Angular Supervision for Visual Object Grounding in Autoregressive Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Autoregressive vision-language models (VLMs) struggle to ground generated text in the correct image regions, and existing explainability methods, such as attention maps and Logit Lens, often produce poor spatial explanations due to weak text-to-vision attention and sink tokens. We propose \textbf{Angular Relevance} ($R_L$), a simple visualization measure based on cosine similarity between visual token embeddings and unembedding-matrix rows. Because $R_L$ is invariant to token norm, it produces substantially sharper and more faithful heatmaps than attention maps or Logit Lens on out-of-the-box models. Without any training, $R_L$ yields competitive referring-expression segmentation (RES), outperforming prior diagnostic maps and CLIP-based training-free methods. To preserve localized object information during cross-modal mixing, we introduce \textbf{Angular Object-Aware Loss (AOL)}, an auxiliary loss that directly supervises visual token embeddings to align angularly with the vocabulary directions of their corresponding object concepts. Finetuning with AOL alongside the standard next-token prediction objective significantly sharpens object localization in heatmaps, showing that the VLM's own visual tokens can be used directly for grounding and improving RES, without training any segmentation heads and without degrading general VQA performance. We further demonstrate that the learned grounding also transfers to category-level segmentation of object categories not seen during training.

AI.brief_summary: 提出基于视觉 token 嵌入与 unembedding 行余弦相似度的 Angular Relevance 度量，并引入角向对象感知辅助损失，直接监督视觉 token 与物体概念词表方向对齐，以改善自回归 VLM 的定位与指代分割。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及视觉细节是否保留在内部状态及训练监督如何塑造这种保留；其无需分割头的 token 级读出与角向监督，可供核查 latent 视觉证据读取、视觉旁路和定位贡献分配。
